characters.name: JC
characters.description: First-person narrator; runs sound at the café open mic, builds the Garden visual, has a nosebleed during the glyph event, taps rhythms on his headboard since age six. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: I ran sound, which is gig-adjacent: Mr. Rodríguez doesn’t pay me, he feeds me.

characters.name: Sofía
characters.description: Sends JC the Early Calm spec; runs an incident-count experiment with a clipboard and clicker at the café versus the bodega control site. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: At the back table she had a clipboard marked INCIDENTS, which she’d defined as a raised voice, a shove, or a slammed anything

characters.name: Mr. Rodríguez
characters.description: Café owner; hosts the open mic, keeps Christmas lights in a NAVIDAD box, calls Manny up to play, son of the Discos Quisqueya record-shop owner. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Mr. Rodríguez clears the tables to the walls and strings up the lights he keeps in a box marked NAVIDAD, in March, because the box is the box.

characters.name: Junior
characters.description: Seventeen; counts bodega incidents with a clicker for twenty bucks and a Pepsi, texting tallies to Sofía. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Junior was seventeen and would have counted anything for twenty bucks and a soda.

characters.name: Doña Fela
characters.description: Mentioned only; bodega neighbor across the street, grandmother of Junior; later reports the block felt something and that her sugar went down.
characters.evidence: “Doña Fela says the whole block felt something at the café,” she said. “She says her sugar went down.”

characters.name: Marisol
characters.description: Sixteen-year-old girl who reads a poem about her father's hands at the open mic. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: A girl named Marisol, sixteen, read a poem about her father’s hands, cracked from the car wash

characters.name: Viejo guitarist
aliases: the viejo nobody had ever seen before
characters.description: Unnamed elderly man who plays a soft bachata on a nylon-string guitar at the open mic. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: A viejo nobody had ever seen before played a bachata on a nylon-string guitar so softly that the espresso machine felt guilty.

characters.name: Kid from Tremont
characters.description: Unnamed young rapper from Tremont whose precise performance earns the older heads' slow nod. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: A kid from Tremont rapped about his block with a precision that made the older heads do the slow nod

characters.name: Teodoro
characters.description: Mr. Rodríguez's friend who reads a twelve-minute poem about a parking ticket with a second act. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Mr. Rodríguez’s friend Teodoro read a twelve-minute poem about a parking ticket.

characters.name: Teodoro's brother-in-law
characters.description: Unnamed audience member who says 'Get to the ticket' at 8:40, logged by Sofía as a raised voice (provoked). Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: At 8:40, Teodoro’s brother-in-law said “Get to the ticket,” out loud.

characters.name: Yari
characters.description: Works nights; texts JC about the wall 'doing a thing' while on hour nine of her shift. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Yari, who works nights and treats the rest of the world as a time zone she’s visiting, texted at 8:55.

characters.name: Yesenia
characters.description: Mentioned only; the scheduled closer, stuck with her violin on the 2 train between stations. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Yesenia and her violin were stuck on the 2 train between stations, which is the kind of problem the 2 train enjoys.

characters.name: Manny
characters.description: Drummer; eats a pastelito, is called up by Mr. Rodríguez, tunes an old conga by ear and plays a set that raises the glyph; invites JC to Rafa's circle. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Then he turned, slowly, toward the back, where Manny was eating a pastelito and not bothering anyone.

characters.name: Mr. Rodríguez's father
characters.description: In the 1986 ECHO: older record-shop owner at Discos Quisqueya, mustache gone to salt, sits with both hands flat on the glass, then hauls up the gate for the bucket-drumming kid. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: At the register sat Mr. Rodríguez’s father, older now, the mustache gone to salt

characters.name: Bucket-drum kid (1986)
characters.description: Unnamed kid in the 1986 ECHO playing a plastic bucket with broom-handle sticks on the curb outside Discos Quisqueya. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: A kid on a plastic bucket, with sticks cut from a broom handle, working a rhythm out on the curb.

characters.name: Old woman at the door
aliases: the woman with the canvas grocery bag
characters.description: Old but not frail, silver hair pulled back hard, cardigan the color of dried tobacco, canvas grocery bag; watches JC rather than the glyph, nods once, and vanishes into the street.
characters.evidence: Silver hair pulled back hard. A cardigan the color of dried tobacco. A canvas grocery bag in one hand

characters.name: Man in the third-floor window
characters.description: Watcher in the blue-netted building across from the café; at a desk with head bowed, arm moving as if writing/counting; looks straight at JC and draws the blind. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: He was at a desk, with his head bowed, and his arm was moving, a small neat motion, the way a man writes when he’s counting.

characters.name: Mamá
characters.description: Sits in the dark kitchen with a rosary wrapped around her fist; wipes the dried blood from JC's lip, feeds him rice and beans, relays Abuela's warning. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Mamá was in the kitchen when I got home, in the dark, at the table, with the rosary wrapped around her fist.

characters.name: Abuela
characters.description: Mentioned only; reportedly tells JC to take care of himself, though Mamá won't say when. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: “Tu abuela dice que te cuides.”

characters.name: Rafa
characters.description: Mentioned only; hosts a drum circle in the park on Sunday that Manny invites JC to.
characters.evidence: “Sunday. Rafa’s circle. In the park. You come. You don’t even have to play.”

characters.name: Open mic audience (ensemble)
characters.description: Collective ensemble of roughly forty café attendees including two babies, arguing bullpen fans, a drinking man, whooping and phone-raising spectators.
characters.evidence: Not one raised voice in a room with forty people, two babies, and a man in the back who’d been drinking since six.

characters.name: Bodega crowd (ensemble)
characters.description: Collective ensemble at the control site across the street; nineteen incidents including a thrown shoe and a domino thrown at a pigeon.
characters.evidence: Nineteen at the bodega. Junior says somebody threw a domino at a pigeon.

scenes.name: Spec discovery, Thursday 11:40 PM
scenes.description: JC studies the crooked scan of the EARLY CALM pilot equipment specification that Sofía sent with no message, with two items circled in red and a blue-ballpoint margin note from someone who had been in those classrooms.
scenes.evidence: Sofía found the spec Thursday night at 11:40 and sent it with no message at all, which from Sofía is a siren.

scenes.name: Building the Garden overnight
scenes.description: Sleepless, JC measures the saved loop (eight seconds, same carrier and pulse as the 1986-era spec) and builds a new visual for Friday's open mic that feeds on noise and turns gray in silence.
scenes.evidence: By the time the 4 had gone past thirty times, I had a new visual for Friday’s open mic, and it ran Item 5 backwards.

scenes.name: Friday café setup and Sofía's experiment
scenes.description: Mr. Rodríguez transforms the café for open mic with NAVIDAD lights and a chalkboard sign; Sofía sets up her INCIDENTS clipboard and clicker while Junior counts at the bodega control site; JC rigs the contact mic and projector.
scenes.evidence: The chalkboard by the door said, in his handwriting, TONIGHT: SOMETHING YOU’VE NEVER SAID OUT LOUD (NO LIMERICKS).

scenes.name: Open mic performances
scenes.description: The Garden turns café noise into spreading color; Marisol reads her poem, the viejo plays bachata, the Tremont kid raps, Teodoro reads his parking-ticket poem, texts arrive from Junior and Yari, and the closer Yesenia is stuck on the 2 train.
scenes.evidence: The Garden fed on everything. Every cup that clinked, every chair that scraped, every laugh turned into color that spread across the brick like spilled ink finding its level.

scenes.name: Manny's conga set and the rising glyph
scenes.description: Mr. Rodríguez calls Manny up; Manny tunes the old conga by ear and plays, the room syncs to him, the Garden goes gold and the spiral-and-triangle glyph rises through it; JC eases the gain down rather than kill it and gets a nosebleed.
scenes.evidence: It rose through the colors like a watermark rising through paper: the spiral and triangle, nested, twenty feet tall, blue and gold, breathing.

scenes.name: ECHO: Discos Quisqueya, 1986
scenes.description: Historical ECHO/vision: the half-gated record shop with peeling paint and flickering fluorescent; Mr. Rodríguez's father sits at the register amid radio reports of shootings, then hears a kid drumming a plastic bucket on the curb and hauls up the gate, spilling light onto the sidewalk.
scenes.evidence: It was Jerome in 1986. The gate was half-down over the shop window, DISCOS QUISQUEYA in peeling paint, one fluorescent tube flickering.

scenes.name: The old woman at the door
scenes.description: After the twenty-six-minute set, JC sees an old woman in a dried-tobacco cardigan with a grocery bag watching him, not the glyph; she nods once like checking a name off a list and leaves; JC chases her out but the street is empty, and the man in the third-floor window looks straight at him and draws the blind.
scenes.evidence: She wasn’t looking at the glyph. She was looking at me.

scenes.name: Curbside aftermath with Sofía and Manny
scenes.description: Sofía sits on the curb with her zero-incident tally and needs a floor; Manny arrives with earned pastelitos, asks whether the wall read his drum or his mind, and invites JC to Rafa's Sunday circle in the park; JC looks at the now-dark window and the spot where the woman stood, and says yeah.
scenes.evidence: “Two incidents at the café in two and a half hours. One of them was the parking ticket. Nineteen at the bodega.

scenes.name: Kitchen with Mamá at midnight
scenes.description: JC comes home to find Mamá in the dark with the rosary around her fist; she relays Doña Fela's report, wipes the dried blood from his lip without asking, feeds him rice and beans, and passes on Abuela's warning without explaining when it was given.
scenes.evidence: She stood, wet a napkin at the sink, and wiped it off, the way she did when I was six and came home with a scraped chin and told her I hadn’t fallen.

scenes.name: Bedroom reflection on the tapping hand
scenes.description: JC lies awake with the blind half down, the radiators knocking and the 4 passing every eight minutes; his hand taps its old rhythm on the headboard and he realizes nobody taught it — it knew what it was up against.
scenes.evidence: It found the headboard. It tapped a small rhythm on the wood, over and over, soft, an old reflex I’d never once thought about.
